The June3,2026 suspension/pass-as-amended question concerns the whole H.R.7618battlefield-grants and two-war-site-study package. It would extend and pool specified authorizations and require qualified studies; passage is not enactment, an actual appropriation, a grant or a park designation. The title's cost-sharing description does not override the operative subsection letters.
The retained308103baseline authorizes$18millionannuallyforacquisition grants through2028, with the stated eligible-battlefield/non-associated-site/outside-NationalPark-boundary conditions and a non-Federal share of at least50percent. The bill changes the authorization endpoint to2036 without changing the$18million amount or those share/site conditions. In308104the bill deletes(d), the separate$1millionauthorization, not(c), the50percentFederal-sharecap for technology-based interpretation/education grants. The restoration program's50percentFederal-sharecap also remains. These share requirements are not repealed by the operative bill.
The bill replaces308105(e)with one shared$2millionannualauthorization for BOTH308104technology-interpretation grants and308105restoration grants throughfiscal2036. It is not$2millioneach or an actual appropriation; the retained separate programs previously each had$1millionauthorization. No unstated first fiscal year for the new through2036language is invented. Existing grant purposes, recipients, site/war qualifications, restoration standards and acquisition land-use restrictions are not silently erased.
Subject to advance appropriations, the SecretaryactingthroughNPSmust prepare or certify studies for nationally significant FrenchAndIndianWar1754–1763andMexicanAmericanWar1846–1848sites/structures in the UnitedStates. The Secretary may prepare them in the stated consultations, or interested parties may prepare them if the Secretary certifies the content requirements are met. Within1yearafterreceivingaprivate-study the Secretary must review/certify WHETHER it meets those requirements; positive certification is not automatic. The content includes identifying sites, relative significance, integrity threats and preservation/interpretation alternatives, potentially including NationalParkSystemdesignation as appropriate, not automatic designation.
Secretary-prepared studies go to the named congressional committees within2yearsafterfundsareavailable; qualifying privately prepared studies go within180daysafterpositivecertification. Neither clock runs simply from enactment. The Secretary must consider and may include earlier studies/reports. Submitted studies are deemed included in BattlefieldReports, but that definition change does not by itself make every studied site eligible for every grant. Existing acquisition battlefield/non-associated-site/NPSboundary gates and the specific RevolutionaryWar/Warof1812/CivilWar limits in the interpretation/restoration eligibility clauses remain unamended; a new two-war study is not automatically a grant award or an eligibility override.
The full captured308101–308106operative unit was read; referenced underlying historic reports, current site status, land-conversion requirements and36CFR68restoration standards were not independently conformed. No current integrated-law or individual-project certificate, new guaranteed funding, technology deployment, restoration result or historical-significance ranking is established.
A Yea supports this whole authorization/study package; a Nay opposes it without a component-specific position or preferred alternative. Infrastructure/Technology membership is an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal tied to the existing explicit technology-deployment interpretation grants and physical battlefield-preservation/restoration framework within the whole measure. A competing boundary treats it as general heritage/cultural conservation and historical study. Independent whole-eligibility/source/taxonomy review is required before acceptance/publication; no accepted domain expansion, motive or realized public outcome follows.
